prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-angled egocentric view of a flat concrete walkway bordered by sand and a raised embankment ahead (roughly 3 to 10+ metres away in frames 4–5), with the camera wearer's lower body at the bottom-left (0.3–1.2 metres away) and a child seated in a stroller directly in front and below the wearer at roughly 0.8–1.5 metres distance (about 0.3–0.5 metres ahead of the wearer's feet, within arm's reach). The child faces forward away from the camera wearer throughout the sequence while holding a small green object within their own reach, and as the wearer walks forward and tilts the camera upward from frame 1 to frame 5, both the wearer's torso and the stroller shift downward and progressively drop out of the bottom of the frame. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated silhouette of the stroller, the hanging pink hat on its right handle, and the child's head and knees from the flat ground plane in frames 1–4. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 1 where the flat ground plane is rendered almost completely black in contrast to the brighter foreground torso, in frame 2 where the wearer's raised right hand at ~0.4 metres on the bottom right is completely missed and blended into the background ground depth, and in frame 5 where the foreground depth saturates into a uniform white band across the bottom edge.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower torso and feet at the bottom-left of frames 1–2 (0.3–1.2 metres from the camera) and the child seated in the stroller directly in front and below the wearer (0.8–1.5 metres away, roughly 0.3–0.5 metres ahead of the wearer's feet and within arm's reach) as separate 'person' masks against the unlabelled walkway and sand background. Across the five frames, as the wearer walks forward and tilts the camera up along the curving path, the wearer's lower body disappears below the bottom edge after frame 2, while the forward-facing child (looking away from the camera wearer) moves toward the bottom center and becomes mostly cropped out by frame 5. The map highlights the exact spatial boundary between the wearer's feet and the rear wheels of the stroller in frame 2, which is harder to separate at a glance in the bright, low-contrast RGB image. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable: it merges the blue stroller and the hanging pink hat into the child's 'person' mask in frames 1–2, misclassifies the wearer's blurred right hand in the bottom-right foreground of frame 2 (at ~0.4 metres, within arm's reach) as a 'carrot', and completely fails to detect the child or stroller in frames 3 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background for the scene where the camera wearer walks behind a forward-facing child seated in a stroller roughly 0.8–1.5 metres ahead and below on a concrete path. Because the child faces away from the camera wearer and is viewed from high above, and the camera wearer's own body is mostly outside the field of view except for the lower torso in frames 1–2 and a raised right hand in frame 2, almost all body and hand joints are self-occluded or cropped by the bottom frame edges as the camera tilts upward across frames 1–5. Where keypoints are detected (in frames 1 and 4), the map attempts to localize the child's seated posture and upper-limb position inside the stroller footprint, which can be difficult to untangle from the stroller frame and clothing in RGB. However, the pose map is largely unreliable across the strip: it completely misses the child in frames 2, 3, and 5 as well as the camera wearer's torso and nearby right hand (at ~0.4 metres in frame 2), while producing a distorted, inverted torso-and-head skeleton on the stroller in frame 1 and spurious yellow body and magenta hand keypoints on the child's lower legs in frame 4.
